title: Postgres cleanup queue handoff and drain (advisory queue)
answers: Is the pg cleanup queue authoritative?
What runs between the ClickHouse sweep and Postgres hard delete?
body:
- `persist_deleted_persons` (dags/clickhouse_cleanup.py) queues swept persons into `person_pg_cleanup_queue` before the step that makes them unrecoverable; one checkpoint covers both PG handoff and CH person delete.
- Queue is advisory: a person can be revived after queueing. `person_pg_cleanup_drain_job` (dags/person_pg_cleanup_drain.py) hands batches to personhog DeleteTombstonedPersons, which deletes only while still tombstoned under row locks; queue row deleted once resolved either way; rows reported blocked get blocked_at.
- Drain pages by primary key keyset (migration rust/persons_migrations/20260910000001_reshape_person_pg_cleanup_queue_for_drain.sql; cleaned_at dropped, deleted_at index unusable for keyset).
- Config bounds: max_runtime_seconds (24h), retry_backoff_seconds, rpc_retry_window_seconds.
- Celery sweeps are only for non-Dagster deployments: `celery_sweeps_enabled` (models/async_deletion/celery_fallback.py; 30-day Dagster activity window) to avoid two sweeps mutating person tables.
